g.text: What it shows: the same measures over Anthropic's two published populations — programmatic API traffic against consumer

text.style: font-size: 10.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: Claude.ai. These are the ten largest gaps, and they are not small: the API is automated, directive and almost entirely

text.style: font-size: 10.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: work, where the consumer product is collaborative, iterative and half personal.

g.text: Note: This is the chart that decides whether a Claude.ai figure may stand in for enterprise behaviour. It may not. Automation runs 94% on

g.text: the API against 49% on Claude.ai, and directive single-shot requests 83% against 31%. Anything estimated from consumer conversation

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: and applied to enterprise workloads inherits that gap. The 1P API file is Anthropic's own API traffic excluding Claude Code,

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 8.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: published globally with no geographic breakdown. It is a different population from Claude.ai and the two are never pooled.
